```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(macodgent)
data(sim_htn_trial)
d <- sim_htn_trial
```

# SIMULATED DATA — read this first

`sim_htn_trial` is **entirely synthetic**. It contains 3000 simulated
hypertension-trial participants and 47 columns, generated by
`data-raw/sim_htn_trial.R` with `set.seed(20261105)`. There are no real
patients, no real trial results and no personally identifiable information.
Every example in this vignette, in the README and in every help page uses
this one dataset. All estimates, p values and survival probabilities below
are artefacts of the simulation; they must not be used for clinical,
regulatory or epidemiological inference.

```{r}
dim(d)
attr(d, "simulated")
attr(d, "provenance")
```

The dataset deliberately contains every variable role the package needs:
continuous and skewed measurements, categorical and ordered factors, binary
and ordinal endpoints, a time-to-event endpoint with a competing cause,
repeated blood-pressure visits in wide format, matched case-control strata,
and MCAR missing values. See `?sim_htn_trial` for the full 47-column
dictionary.

# 1. Data overview

```{r}
mc_inspect(d[, c("id", "age", "bmi", "smoke", "crp")], detailed = TRUE)
mc_stat_mode(d$site)
```

# 2. Quantitative and qualitative description

```{r}
mc_describe_numeric(d, vars = c("age", "bmi", "sbp_baseline"),
                    group = "treatment")
mc_test_normality(d$crp)
mc_correlate(d, vars = c("age", "bmi", "sbp_baseline", "ldl", "glucose"))
```

# 3. Group comparison and Table One

```{r}
mc_compare_groups(d, group = "treatment",
                  vars = c("age", "bmi", "crp", "smoke", "sex"))
mc_baseline_table(d, vars = c("age", "bmi", "sex", "smoke", "sbp_baseline"),
                  group = "treatment")
```

# 4. Logistic screening and full diagnostic report

```{r}
sc <- mc_logistic_screen(d, y = "bp_control",
  x_vars = c("age", "bmi", "ldl", "glucose", "smoke", "diabetes"),
  p_adjust = "BH")
sc$univariate
rep <- mc_logistic_report(d,
  bp_control ~ age + bmi + treatment + diabetes, auc_boot = 0L)
rep$checks
```

# 5. Survival analysis

```{r}
km <- mc_kaplan_meier(d, time = "followup_days", status = "cv_event",
                      group = "treatment")
km$logrank
cox <- mc_cox(d, survival::Surv(followup_days, cv_event) ~
                age + bmi + treatment + diabetes)
cox$performance
```

# 6. Non-linear dose-response

```{r}
rcs <- mc_rcs(d, x = "sbp_baseline", y = "sbp_week12", nk = 4)
rcs$nonlinearity_p
head(rcs$curve)
```

# 7. One call, many results

```{r}
auto <- mc_auto_analyze(d, outcome = "bp_control", group = "treatment",
  vars = c("age", "bmi", "sbp_baseline", "ldl", "glucose", "smoke", "diabetes"),
  auc_boot = 0L)
auto$findings
auto$model$checks
```

The mapping between each function and the analysis modules is listed in the
module table of `README.md`.
